draft.title: Renewable and non-renewable resources
card: Resource
A resource is something from the natural environment that people use, such as water, soil, timber or coal.
Renewable
a resource that can be replaced by natural processes within a human lifetime. Sunlight, wind and forests are examples.
Non-renewable
a resource that takes millions of years to form, so it runs out once it is used. Coal, oil and natural gas are examples.
A renewable resource can still be used up if people take it faster than it is replaced. A forest cleared faster than it regrows is one case.
draft.remember: Renewable resources are replaced in a human lifetime, but only if use does not outpace replacement.

a.q: Why is coal called a non-renewable resource?
opts: It takes millions of years to form, so it cannot be replaced
It is dug from the ground, which damages the land
It produces smoke when it is burned for energy
It can only be used by large power stations
a.why: Coal forms over millions of years, far longer than a human lifetime, so once it is burned it is gone for practical purposes. Damage from mining is a different issue and does not decide whether a resource is renewable.
a.clue: Think about how long coal takes to form.

b.q: A timber company in Tasmania cuts trees from a forest much faster than they regrow. What is the best description of the forest?
opts: Renewable, but being used faster than it is replaced
Non-renewable, because trees die once they are cut
Non-renewable, because the forest is owned by a company
Renewable, so it cannot be used up however fast it is cut
b.why: Forests can regrow within a human lifetime, so they are renewable. If trees are cut faster than they regrow, the supply can still run down. The last option is wrong because renewable does not mean it cannot be used up.
b.clue: Consider both how the forest is replaced and how fast it is used.

a.best: It takes millions of years to form, so it cannot be replaced

b.best: Renewable, but being used faster than it is replaced

problems.detail: The remember line uses 'only' ('but only if use does not outpace replacement') where the card says a renewable resource 'can still be used up'. Its phrasing also suggests renewable resources are replaced only under a condition, which is less clear than the card.
The clue 'Think about how long coal takes to form' points straight to the only option about formation time, so students can pick it without understanding the idea.

check.summary: The facts are correct and both questions have one clear right answer. However, question a's clue gives the answer away, and the remember line uses 'only' where the card says 'can'.

a.q: Why is coal called a non-renewable resource?
